title.narrative: Conserving the Paraguayan Chaco for the benefit of jaguars and for people

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Strengthening enabling environments to support a healthy Jaguar population in Chaco Biosphere Reserve while benefiting the local communities living in the landscape, through reforms to the policy and regulatory frameworks, enhanced management of human-wildlife interactions, the promotion of behavior change in communities and private landowners, and knowledge sharing.

This project will deliver direct and indirect benefits to: communities and individuals in buffer zones of the three prioritized protected areas in the Chaco Region; and primarily in the municipalities of Bahia Negra, Fuerte Olimpo, Mariscal Estigarribia, Filadelfia, Boquerón, Alto Paraguay, plus the Ñu Guazu, Pycasu, and Siracua Indigenous People communities, targeting in total 1,500 women and 3,500 men. Enhanced management effectiveness of protected areas and improved practices in landscapes will help to secure the ecosystems and associated goods and services these systems provide to local communities and the broader society in terms of water security, food, medicine, fuel, food, clean air, and carbon sequestration. Indigenous communities will benefit directly from three diversified livelihood programmes in terms of capacity building and start-up support, with a view to reduce their reliance on the extractive use of natural resources as their sole source of income. The Private Sector will benefit from the implementation of jaguar-centric cattle ranching practices, through ten (10) custom-designed management plans that meet the particular needs of each ranch, and in the adoption and application of market-based incentives for the conservation of jaguars in productive areas of the buffer zones of protected areas in the Chaco Biosphere Reserve, in the implementation of non-lethal strategies for conflict reduction, and from the demonstration of the economic feasibility of non-lethal methods of control. Staff of the Directorate of Protected Areas within MADES will benefit from enhanced capacity building for the management of protected areas, as well as at the institutional level in terms of reforms to the legal framework to facilitate their work in protected areas management. Enforcement officers (police and military) will benefit from gender-balanced training in evidence gathering and other associated disciplines to address wildlife crimes, and prosecutors and judges will benefit from gender-balanced training in case file preparation, case management, legal interpretation, and other associated disciplines for the successful prosecution of wildlife crimes.
